6º de Primaria · Inglés · Tema 3

Comparatives and superlatives

Nombre: ______________________   Fecha: ___________

Qué vas a aprender

  • Compare two things with comparatives: taller than, more expensive than
  • Say which is the top one in a group with superlatives: the tallest, the most expensive
  • Use the irregular forms good, bad and far
  • Compare people, animals and places in short texts
  • Compare with less and the least
  • Make comparisons stronger or softer: much better, a bit taller
  • Use too and enough
  • Compare actions with adverbs and compare two countries

Para pensar

Un guepardo es más rápido que un caballo. Pero ¿cuál es el animal terrestre más rápido de todos? ¿Cómo dirías «más rápido que» y «el más rápido» en inglés?

Explicación

1. Comparing two or more

When we compare two things we use the comparative: «A horse is bigger than a dog». When we choose the number one in a group of three or more we use the superlative: «The elephant is the biggest of the three».

En castellano: el comparativo es «más… que» y el superlativo es «el más… de». En inglés, el adjetivo cambia: big → bigger → the biggest. Detrás del comparativo va than («que») y delante del superlativo va the.

2. Short adjectives: -er and -est

Adjectives with one syllable add -er and -est: tall → taller → the tallest; fast → faster → the fastest; old → older → the oldest; small → smaller → the smallest.

Spelling: ending in -e, add only -r / -st: nice → nicer → the nicest. Consonant + vowel + consonant, double the letter: big → bigger → the biggest; hot → hotter → the hottest; thin → thinner → the thinnest.

3. Adjectives ending in -y

Adjectives with two syllables that end in -y change the y to -ier and -iest: happy → happier → the happiest; funny → funnier → the funniest; easy → easier → the easiest; heavy → heavier → the heaviest.

Example: «My cat is lazier than my dog, but my hamster is the laziest pet in the house!». En castellano: es la misma regla de la y que en el pasado (study → studied): la y se convierte en i.

4. Long adjectives: more and the most

Long adjectives (two or more syllables, not ending in -y) don't change. We put more or the most before them: interesting → more interesting → the most interesting; expensive → more expensive → the most expensive; beautiful, dangerous, important, popular…

«A tiger is more dangerous than a cat». «The blue whale is the most amazing animal I know». Never mix the two forms: not «more bigger» or «the most fastest».

5. Less and the least

We usually compare things by saying that one has more of a quality. But we can also say that it has less:

  • less + adjective + than: «This film is less interesting than the book.» (menos interesante que)
  • the least + adjective: «Maths is the least difficult subject for me.» (la menos difícil)

With short adjectives, it is more natural to use not as … as: «My bike isn't as fast as yours» sounds better than «My bike is less fast than yours».

Less and fewer are also used with nouns:

  • fewer + countable nouns: «I have fewer books than you.»
  • less + uncountable nouns: «There is less water in this bottle.»

And the opposites with more: «I have more books / more water than you.» In everyday English, many people say «less books», but in correct written English we use fewer with countable nouns.

6. Irregular forms

Three very common adjectives are irregular: good → better → the best; bad → worse → the worst; far → further → the furthest.

«This pizza is better than the last one». «It was the best day of my life!». «Monday is the worst day of the week». En castellano: también en español son irregulares: bueno → mejor (no «más bueno»), malo → peor. Por eso en inglés nunca se dice «gooder» ni «the goodest».

7. Much better, a bit taller

We can make a comparison stronger or softer by adding a word before the comparative:

  • A big difference: much, a lot, far. «An elephant is much heavier than a mouse.» «Your drawing is a lot better than mine.» «The sun is far bigger than the Earth.»
  • A small difference: a bit, a little, slightly. «I'm a bit taller than my sister.» «Today is a little warmer than yesterday.»

Be careful: we can't use very with comparatives. «Very taller» is wrong. Use much taller.

With superlatives, we can use by far or one of:

  • «She is by far the best player in the team.» (con diferencia la mejor)
  • «It's one of the most beautiful places in the world.» Notice: one of the + superlative + plural noun.

And we can say that something keeps changing with two comparatives: «It's getting colder and colder.» «The film was more and more exciting.»

8. Superlatives in sentences

After a superlative we often say the group with in (places, groups) or of (a number or time): «Mount Everest is the highest mountain in the world», «Ana is the tallest girl in my class», «It's the coldest day of the year».

We can also use the present perfect phrase I've ever (que he… nunca): «It's the best book I've ever read». En castellano: «el mejor libro que he leído nunca».

9. As … as: the same

To say two things are equal (iguales) we use as + adjective + as: «My brother is as tall as my dad». In the negative, not as … as means «less»: «A bike isn't as fast as a car».

Compare these sentences, they mean the same: «A car is faster than a bike» = «A bike isn't as fast as a car». En castellano: «as… as» es «tan… como». El adjetivo va en su forma normal, sin -er.

10. Too and enough

Too and enough are not comparatives, but they also talk about «how much» of a quality something has.

  • too + adjective = more than necessary, a problem (demasiado): «This T-shirt is too big for me.» «It's too cold to go swimming.»
  • adjective + enough = the right amount (suficientemente): «Is the water warm enough?» «She's old enough to go alone.» Notice the order: enough goes after the adjective.
  • not + adjective + enough = less than necessary: «I'm not tall enough to reach the shelf.»

With nouns, enough goes before: «We have enough chairs.» «There isn't enough time.» And too becomes too much or too many: «There is too much noise.» «There are too many people.»

Compare: «The box is too heavy, I can't carry it» and «The box is light enough, I can carry it».

11. Reading: world records

Read about animal records: «The biggest animal in the world is the blue whale. It is heavier than thirty elephants! The cheetah is the fastest land animal: it is faster than a car in the city. The giraffe is the tallest animal, and its tongue is longer than your arm. Tortoises are slower than most animals, but some live longer than people. Which animal do you think is the most interesting?»

12. Let's practise: class records

Make a class record book in groups. Measure and ask: «Who is the tallest?», «Who has the longest name?», «Who lives the furthest from school?». Write the results: «Pablo is the tallest. His name is shorter than Alejandro's».

Then compare two places you know: your town and a big city. «My town is smaller and quieter than Barcelona, but Barcelona is more exciting». Consejo: cuenta las sílabas del adjetivo antes de elegir -er o more.

13. Comparing actions

We can also compare how people do things. For this we use adverbs:

  • Short adverbs, which have the same form as the adjective, add -er and -est: fast → faster → the fastest; hard → harder → the hardest; early → earlier → the earliest. «Sara runs faster than Leo.» «Who gets up the earliest in your family?»
  • Adverbs ending in -ly use more and the most: carefully → more carefully → the most carefully; slowly → more slowly; quietly → more quietly. «Please speak more slowly.» «Lucía writes the most carefully in the class.»
  • Irregular adverbs: well → better → the best; badly → worse → the worst. «She sings better than me.» «I played worse today.»

Remember the difference between an adjective and an adverb: «He is a good singer» (adjective) but «He sings well» (adverb). «She is a careful driver» but «She drives carefully».

14. Spain and the UK

Let's compare two European countries: Spain and the United Kingdom.

  • Size: Spain is much bigger than the UK. It is about 506,000 km², more than twice as big as the UK (about 243,000 km²).
  • Population: the UK has more people: about 69 million. Spain has about 49 million. So the UK is more crowded.
  • Mountains: the highest mountain in Spain is the Teide, in Tenerife (3,715 m). The highest in the UK is Ben Nevis, in Scotland (1,345 m). The Teide is far higher!
  • Capitals: London is bigger than Madrid. It has about 9 million people; Madrid has about 3.4 million.
  • Weather: Spain is usually sunnier, hotter and drier than the UK, especially in summer. The UK is rainier and cloudier, but its summers are cooler and more comfortable for many people.
  • Dinner time: people in the UK usually have dinner much earlier than people in Spain!

Now choose two places you know, like two towns or two countries, and write five comparisons. Use numbers when you can: real facts and data make your comparisons much stronger and more interesting for the reader.

15. The more, the better

There is a special structure with two comparatives that shows how one thing changes together with another: the + comparative …, the + comparative …

  • «The more you read, the more you learn.» (Cuanto más lees, más aprendes.)
  • «The older I get, the taller I am.»
  • «The faster you run, the sooner you arrive.»
  • «The less you sleep, the more tired you feel.»
  • «The higher you climb, the colder it gets.»

There is also a very common short expression: «The more, the merrier!» It means that more people make a party or an activity more fun. You can say it when a friend asks if they can join your game: «Can I play with you?» – «Of course! The more, the merrier!» And «the sooner, the better» means that something should happen as soon as possible.

En castellano usamos «cuanto más…, más…»: «Cuanto más practicas, mejor juegas» = «The more you practise, the better you play».

Try to complete these sentences about yourself: «The more I play video games, the…» «The more I practise English, the…»

Comparatives and superlatives

Ejercicios

  1. Write the comparative: cold, nice, big, happy.

  2. Write the superlative: small, funny, expensive, good.

  3. Complete: «A mouse is (small) ___ a cat.»

  4. Complete: «August is (hot) ___ month of the year.»

  5. Complete: «Football is (popular) ___ handball in Spain.»

  6. Correct: «My bike is more good than yours.»

  7. Rewrite with as … as: «Tom is 12. Ana is 12.» (old)

  8. Rewrite with not as … as: «A car is faster than a bike.»

  9. Translate: «Es el peor día de la semana.»

  10. Compare three animals in three sentences.

  11. Complete: «This book is ___ interesting than that one.» (less)

  12. Choose: «I'm (a bit / very) taller than my brother.»

  13. Complete: «The soup is too ___ (hot) to eat.»

  14. Write the comparative of the adverb: fast, well.

  15. Which is bigger, Spain or the UK?

  16. Order the words: enough / not / I'm / tall.

  17. Fewer or less? «There is ___ milk.» «There are ___ apples.»

  18. Write a sentence with «one of the most…».

  19. Correct: «She speaks more good than me.»

  20. Who won the race in the twins' story?

  21. Compare two classmates' abilities using three adverbs (politely!).

  22. Write three sentences with too and three with enough about your school.

  23. Compare your town with another town (five sentences, with much and a bit).

  24. Explain the difference between «He is a good singer» and «He sings well».

Practica

  1. The comparative of «tall» is…

    1. A) more tall
    2. B) taller
    3. C) tallest

  2. The superlative of «big» is…

    1. A) the bigest
    2. B) the most big
    3. C) the biggest

  3. The comparative of «easy» is…

    1. A) easier
    2. B) easyer
    3. C) more easy

  4. The superlative of «beautiful» is…

    1. A) the beautifulest
    2. B) the more beautiful
    3. C) the most beautiful

  5. The comparative of «good» is…

    1. A) gooder
    2. B) better
    3. C) best

  6. The superlative of «bad» is…

    1. A) the worst
    2. B) the baddest
    3. C) the worse

  7. «Spain is bigger ___ Portugal.»

    1. A) that
    2. B) than
    3. C) as

  8. «It's the longest river ___ Spain.»

    1. A) of
    2. B) than
    3. C) in

  9. «Tan rápido como» is…

    1. A) as fast as
    2. B) so fast than
    3. C) as faster as

  10. Which sentence is correct?

    1. A) He is funniest boy in class.
    2. B) He is the funniest boy in class.
    3. C) He is the most funny boy in class.

  11. «This is ___ difficult exercise of all.»

    1. A) less
    2. B) the least
    3. C) the less

  12. «An elephant is ___ heavier than a dog.»

    1. A) very
    2. B) too
    3. C) much

  13. «Is the room big ___ for the party?»

    1. A) too
    2. B) enough
    3. C) much

  14. «She works ___ than me.»

    1. A) harder
    2. B) more hard
    3. C) hardlier

  15. The highest mountain in Spain is…

    1. A) Ben Nevis
    2. B) the Mulhacén
    3. C) the Teide

Explícalo con tus palabras

Incluye: Diferencia entre comparativo y superlativo; Cuándo se usa -er/-est y cuándo more/the most; Cuáles son los irregulares good, bad y far; Cómo se dice «tan… como» en inglés.
